name: Positioning Test and Messaging Execution

positioning.oneLineSummary: Tests positioning in structured live conversations with best-fit prospects, then governs translation into consistent messaging.
positioning.productLabel: Positioning Test-and-Execution Lens — based on April Dunford's 2026 public materials
notAClaimOf: sales-pitch quality being the same as positioning quality

attribution.display: Based on April Dunford's 2026 public materials

neutralParaphrase: Translate the positioning chain into a structured sales conversation and test it with best-fit prospects, observing comprehension, relevance, objections, progression, and losses. After learning, create a governed messaging document for consistency; do not rely on homepage experiments that combine many uncontrolled variables.

locator.value: 03:25-21:25, homepage-test limits, live conversations, sales pitch, messaging document, revisit triggers
Expanded post-positioning, sales-pitch testing, and messaging section
Positioning as GTM foundation and sales-pitch relation

requiredConditions: OA2-07 has produced a positioning hypothesis.
Best-fit prospects and actual sellers are available.
Test scripts, versions, and outcomes can be recorded lawfully.

requiredEvidence.description: Versioned pitch, best-fit criteria, seller guidance, observation fields, sample, and comparison plan.
Comprehension, value recognition, alternatives, objections, next-step conversion, and qualitative loss reasons.
Approved claims, proof, audience, prohibited claims, asset mapping, version, owner, and review triggers.

decisionQuestions: Do best-fit prospects understand the context and differentiated value in live conversation?
Which link fails when deals do not progress?
Are seller, segment, pricing, or product variables confounding the test?
Does the messaging document preserve evidence and prevent claim drift?
positiveSignals: Best-fit prospects consistently understand and restate the value.
Progression improves without hiding objections or changing qualification.
Loss evidence produces targeted component revisions.
Messaging claims remain versioned, sourced, and consistent.
redFlags: One homepage metric is treated as positioning validation.
Tests mix different segments, sellers, prices, and messages.
Messaging adds unsupported claims after the positioning exercise.
disconfirmingEvidence: Comprehension improves but commercial progression does not.
A strong seller compensates for weak positioning.
A weak pitch obscures an otherwise sound positioning chain.
Consistent messaging repeats a wrong market assumption.
contraindications: Do not claim causal validation from uncontrolled conversations.
Do not treat messaging consistency as truth.
Do not expose confidential customer conversations without permission.

instructions: Version the positioning and sales-test protocol.
Review full outcomes including losses and no-decisions.
Separate positioning from seller, price, product, and process confounds.
Conclude supported, needs component revision, test-confounded, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not calculate test effects or claim causality.

sourceReliability.medium: Recorded calls and CRM with some controls.
sourceReliability.high: Versioned calls, CRM, win/loss, seller, and customer evidence converge.

evidenceStrength.high: Repeated best-fit outcomes with plausible confounds addressed.

evidenceCoverage.high: Wins, losses, no-decision, segments, sellers, versions, objections, and confounds covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: Live sales conversation is a material acquisition mechanism.

empiricalQualifications: Live tests are observational unless designed otherwise.
Sales outcomes depend on many non-positioning variables.

rights.notes: Author's public 2026 post-positioning guidance is neutrally paraphrased.

openIssues: Review licensed post-work chapter and define minimum test protocol.
